purpose: The public face of this organisation keeps understating what the implementation repositories can prove. On 2026-11-24 that happened three times in one day: a second implementation (verify-js, 18 of 19 checks) was described as missing; a verifier benchmark record was described as absent; and a Bitcoin block attestation (height 976735) was described as pending. Each description was written from memory or from an older snapshot. This file exists so that a claim about our own state is a row with a digest behind it, and so that 'absent' has to survive a file that says otherwise.
rules: present: at least one witness whose bytes are fetched and whose sha256 and length are compared; at least one of them must not be prose (.md/.txt), because a paragraph cannot witness itself.

absent: must carry an absent_check that fetches a machine-readable ledger and compares a path to an expected value. If the ledger says otherwise, the entry is refused - that is how an under-claim is stopped.
link: where one witness states the digest of another (a proof file naming its own container), the two must agree.
as_of: an ISO date for when the claim was last re-derived from the artifacts rather than remembered.

entries.claim: The public corpus gate has eight rows, each pinned to an expected verdict and exit code, and a drifted cell fails the build.
entries.measured: MATRIX GATE OK - all 8 rows match (local; CI green on 2 OS x 2 Python)

entries.claim: Twelve adversarial packages are built at run time; nine must be refused, three are documented defects that must still reproduce.
entries.measured: ADVERSARIAL OK - 9/9 must-reject cases rejected; 3 documented gap(s) still reproduce

entries.claim: The committed fixture bytes are pinned by digest, so a fixture cannot be edited to make a case pass.
entries.measured: FROZEN OK - 45 fixture files match FIXTURES.sha256

entries.claim: A submission registry exists with six states, transitions enforced by a script, and honest zero independent rows.
entries.measured: REGISTRY OK - 1 entry, 0 independent, transitions valid; NEGATIVE CONTROL OK - 4/4 bad inputs rejected

entries.claim: A second implementation in a second language exists and is enforced in CI, covering 18 of 19 checks.
entries.measured: strict 36/36, refused 30/36 over 36 packages; tools/assert_second_impl.py fails the build when the second implementation drifts
entries.why_it_matters: Public documents described this as missing on 2026-11-24 while the code had been in CI since 2026-11-18. An under-claim is as damaging as an overclaim when a reader relies on it.

entries.claim: A separate verifier has been measured against the mutation benchmark, with per-case raw exit codes recorded.
The v0.5.0 corpus digest file is attested by a Bitcoin block, not merely by a calendar server.
entries.measured: block height 976735, block time 2026-11-20T14:17:33Z, merkle root matched against blockstream.info on 2026-11-21T01:15Z

link.note: the attestation names the digest of its own proof container

entries.limits: A block proves existence before that block's time. It does not prove authorship, and it does not prove the workflow behaved.

entries.claim: The v0.4.1 corpus digest file is attested by a Bitcoin block.

link.note: the v0.4.1 page file was a bare serialized tree the ots client refuses, so the standard container lives in the repository

entries.claim: No run of this corpus by anyone outside this organisation has been posted.

absent_check.note: if this ledger ever shows a headline above zero, this entry is wrong and the checker refuses it

entries.limits: Absence is the one claim this file cannot make cheaply: a ledger we maintain could simply never be updated. It is recorded as a machine-checked zero, not as proof that nobody ran it.
